children: By Samuel Indyk
Short-dated euro zone government bond yields were higher on Thursday, a day after the Federal Reserve raised its interest rate and signalled further increases to curb inflation.

The Fed raised the benchmark overnight interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point to the 3.75-4% range, its first increase in three years, while its projections showed a majority of policymakers anticipate at least one more hike by the end of the year.
"I think the message was clear that there's going to be more hiking," said Jan von Gerich, chief analyst at Nordea.
"The message was on the hawkish side, there's no question about that."
The size and importance of the U.S. economy and the influence of the Federal Reserve on other central banks mean U.S. monetary policy tends to affect global bond markets.
Germany's 10-year bond yield (DE10YT=RR), the benchmark for the euro zone, was up 1.5 basis points (bps) to 3.526%, just below its 17-year peak of 3.5723% hit on Tuesday.
The move in bonds was more evident at the policy-sensitive shorter end of the curve, where Germany's 2-year yield (DE2YT=RR) was up 3.5 bps to 3.247%. Bond yields move inversely with prices.
The U.S. 2-year yield (US2YT=RR) rose to its highest in over two years after the Fed decision but was slightly lower on Thursday at 4.715%.
ENERGY REMAINS IN FOCUS

As the Fed grabbed the headlines on Wednesday, investors in Europe also watched high oil and gas prices, which have raised the risk that the European Central Bank will have to increase interest rates again.
Brent crude futures
have edged lower in the last two days but remain above $104 per barrel, keeping inflation concerns simmering.
"We would need to see a quick fall in energy prices to prevent another ECB hike," Nordea's Von Gerich said.
The ECB last week raised its deposit rate for a second time this year as it attempts to quell an energy-driven rise in inflation.
Headline consumer prices rose 3.2% from a year ago in August, revised data from the EU statistics office Eurostat showed on Thursday, above the ECB's 2% target.
Markets are pricing in a greater-than-40% chance of a rate hike from the ECB at its October meeting, while three quarter-point hikes are fully priced in by June of next year.
